- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior 7-day average.
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from 7-day high), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 10% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 3–8% to avoid overbought signals.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment oscillating 0.4–0.6), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% to match recent momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward moves after prolonged high sentiment; add 1–3% buffer to true outcome if sentiment drops below 0.4.
- If sentiment is near zero (0.0–0.1) and price is falling, model underestimates further decline; forecast should be 2–5% below true outcome to capture bearish momentum.
